question:
One way of measuring a person’s body fat content is by “weighing” them under water. This works because fat tends to float on water as it is less dense than water. On the other hand muscle and bone tend to sink as they are more dense. Knowing your “weight” under water as well as your real weight out of water, the percentage of your body’s volume that is made up of fat can easily be estimated. This is only an estimate since it assumes that your body is made up of only two substances, fat (low density) and everything else (high density). The “weight” is measured by spring balance both inside and outside the water. Quotes are placed around weight to indicate that the measurement read on the scale is not your true weight, i.e. the force applied to your body by gravity, but a measurement of the net downward force on the scale.

Ram and Shyam are having the same weight when measured outside the water. When measured under water, it is found that weight of Ram is more than that of Shyam, then we can say that

options.A: Ram is having more fat content than Shyam.
options.B: Shyam is having more fat content that Ram.
options.C: Ram and Shyam both are having the same fat content.
